blocks.content: As the Earth rotates from west to east, places located east of Greenwich see the sun earlier than places to the west.

rows: Time determined according to the position of the sun at a specific local meridian.

items: Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated from 82°30' E longitude and is exactly 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT (+5:30).
The longitudinal spread of India is nearly 30°, resulting in a 2-hour local time difference between Arunachal Pradesh in the east and Gujarat in the west.
The Standard Meridian of India (82°30' E) passes through Mirzapur (UP) and covers 5 states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Local time is determined by the position of the overhead sun at a specific meridian of longitude.
The Earth completes one rotation of 360° in 24 hours, which equals 15° per hour or 1° every 4 minutes.
Because Earth rotates from west to east, local time moves ahead towards the east and lags towards the west.
All places located on the same meridian of longitude share the exact same local time.
To prevent confusion caused by differing local times across longitudes, countries adopt a single Standard Time based on a central meridian.
